score.note: First pass, recovered directly from games/gs1/asm/080da2ac.s (hand-decoded literal pools by computing every pc-relative ldr's target address against the two .4byte pools) plus the m2c-assisted context in out/family-transplants/main-080da2ac/m2c/ (target.canonical.s, target.lst with resolved hex offsets, and the m2c decompile used only as a structural cross-check, not copied verbatim -- its own call modeling of the trampoline sites and its sp-offset variable names do not match the real stack frame and were not trusted). The family-matcher's template (main:080ce85c, score 8145/10000) is a structural false-positive for the algorithm: this owner shares the 0x03001eec battle-work prologue idiom, field offsets (0x7780/0x7784/0x7824/0x7828/0x77A8), and several callees with the template, but is a different sub-effect entirely (a variant-driven shrinking/expanding horizontal bar wipe read from a 3-byte-per-entry table at 0x080eea38, not an orbiting-sprite animation) -- confirmed structurally correct against 080d82b0.c/080e01e4.c/080d59b0.c, the other already-measured siblings of this same battle-work family, whose dossiers document the same template mismatch and the same open residuals hit here. Two Func_08007xxx call sites are the r3 and r4 entries of the _call_via_rN trampoline at games/gs1/asm/080072e4.s (0x080072f0 = r3, 0x080072f4 = r4): the r3 site is modeled as the already-established `Func_080072f0(dest, src, size, (WordCopyFn)0x03001388)` direct-call-with-trailing-target-argument idiom (from 080d82b0.c); the two r4 sites are modeled as a genuinely traced `DrawRectangleFn draw_rectangle_fn = *(DrawRectangleFn*)((u8*)heap_cache + 28);` (== *(DrawRectangleFn*)0x03001F08, the same heap_cache+0x1C slot 080d82b0.json independently derived and confirmed) called directly as `draw_rectangle_fn(dest, src, x, y, w, h)`. The Func_080e0524 id argument uses the already-established `(s32)&Value_0000008b` pool-forcing idiom (0x8B does not compile to a movs immediate at its call site in the reference, matching the pattern documented in 080e01e4.json/member_orbit's Value_000000af). candidate-show --align confirms the algorithm/control-flow shape is correct: instruction counts are close (455 candidate vs 462 reference insns) and several structural landmarks now match byte-for-byte, including the reference's exact 116-byte stack frame (`sub sp,#116`, matched after adding an explicit `bounds_ptr = bounds;` local to reproduce the reference's real stack-spilled cache of the 4-word bounds-table base address -- omitting it left the frame 4 bytes short), the whole 16-byte Bounds4 struct-copy prologue from 0x080eda88 (ldmia r3!,{r0,r1,r4}/stmia r2!,{r0,r1,r4}/ldr/str, identical registers), and the `screen`/`position` 12-byte local array addresses (sp+76 and sp+88) landing at the reference's exact offsets. The residual differing_halfwords is now dominated by one recurring, already cross-family-documented open register-allocation question (see notes): the reference keeps `work` (the 0x03001EEC-rooted battle-work pointer) resident in r9 for the entire function and computes work-relative field addresses as a single `add rX, r9` from a pc-relative immediate at every use site; this compiler's allocator instead spills `work` to a stack slot here and reloads+adds it (two instructions, same total cost, different registers/offsets) at nearly every one of the ~15 M2C_FIELD(work,...,0x7828) style accesses, which cascades into differing register choices and stack-slot numbers through most of the rest of the function even though the values and control flow are correct. Tried and confirmed not source-shape-controllable per the ban on register forcing: giving the work+0x7828 dereference its own function-scope `void *effect` local (reassigned fresh at each use site, mirroring 080d82b0.c's `target` idiom) regressed the score (differing_halfwords 512->514, wrong_instructions 466->562) rather than helping, and was reverted in favor of inline nested M2C_FIELD(M2C_FIELD(work,...),...) expressions at each site. Splitting the initial 16x40 pixel-copy loop's shared `i`/`j` counters into loop-unique names (row_i/col_j) plus giving the three later do-while loops (zero-init, member-position, member-flag) their own unique counter identities instead of a shared `i` also regressed slightly (differing_halfwords 512->514) and was reverted back to the shared-`i` baseline, which scored best. Declaration-order swap of the bottom three locals (bounds before position before screen, matching the frame allocator's documented first-declared-highest-address rule for same-size-class locals) measurably helped once combined with the bounds_ptr fix. Still not exact.

Semantic summary: a battle-presentation sub-effect on the shared 0x03001eec battle-work block. Sets BG2 affine scale/rotation registers, builds a 640-byte (16x40) sub-rectangle copy of a tiled bitmap at 0x02010000 into the work block, conditionally flips a BG3 affine register and sets a -112 x-offset correction for one orientation of the effect's owner object, opens display window kind 46, reads a DrawRectangleFn pointer out of the shared heap_cache+0x1C slot, zero-initializes one field of each party member's per-effect record, registers a scheduler callback, copies a 16-byte ROM constant into a local 4-word 'bounds' table, and then runs a variant-selected number of frames (looked up from a 3-byte-per-entry table at 0x080eea38 indexed by the owner object's field 0x18). Each frame advances a 3-band scanning window over the bounds table (periodically bumping one band's stored value by 32), and once the frame counter enters a band's active window, computes a sine-scaled bar half-height and draws two fixed-width (40px) rectangles of varying height, then scans every party member: projecting each member's 3D position to screen space, flagging members whose projected position falls inside the just-drawn bar's bounds (setting two fields on the member object), and cueing a status callback for any member whose field-12 value has gone negative. After the 3-band loop, a second per-member pass fires a one-shot Func_080d6888 cue for any member whose per-effect record flag is still unset and whose object fields indicate an out-of-battle/negative-value state. Ends by unregistering the scheduler callback and freeing window kind 46.

The dominant residual, consistent with every other measured owner in this same 0x03001eec battle-work family (080d59b0.json, 080d82b0.json, 080e01e4.json, 080dc1ec.json), is the compiler's register-allocation priority choosing to spill the long-lived `work` pointer to a stack slot and reload+add it at each use, where the reference instead keeps it resident in r9 for the whole function. Per the ban on forcing register assignment via source tricks, and per the precedent in the sibling dossiers (declaration-order and scoping levers tried there had zero effect on this same fp/r9-class choice), this was not chased further with blind lever-pulling here beyond the two declaration-order experiments recorded above. Everything else -- the algorithm, every field offset, every table/constant value, every call argument, the trampoline-call modeling, and the exact 116-byte stack frame shape -- is confirmed correct against the retained assembly.
No GS2 or external source was used; no other Golden Sun decompilation project was consulted.
